method: Read-only final source and owner API contract review. This review starts no build, GUI, instrument, network or resource measurement.
verification_status_at_review: The initial independent checkpoint was superseded by visual-source fixes. Root is rerunning fresh clean serial verification; final results must be read from current verification.json and hashed logs. Superseded checkpoint/screenshots are retained under pre_visual_fix, and this review does not promote those results to the changed source.
static_observations: New point rows no longer fabricate a 1:1 dilution ratio; dilution labels and numeric cells require explicit entry.
Store numeric validation and page input both enforce nonnegative finite values no greater than99999 and no more than4 decimal places, with binary representation tolerance only in storage validation.
checkCatalog rejects missing/changed Calibration unit or ratio and missing/changed Original result unit; batch stable ID, project, code and component-group identity are checked.

writeRecord checks immutable saved identity, including project, batch, calibrator batch, method, transforms, axis units/ratio and copy source; revision changes cannot silently reassign a historical record.
Dirty record selection remains in project list after catalog removal, and the new-record modal marks busy and rechecks project/session identity before retaining a draft.

Request IDs reject stale catalog/record results, repeated reload is bounded while busy/dirty, worker SQL is created/used/closed in its owning thread, and local write transactions preserve base/point consistency.

Raw scatter shows concentration on x and arithmetic raw-test mean on y. Fitting, inverse calculation, audit/application, method mutation and task waveform actions remain disabled; local schema rejects checked/applied values.

CalibrationStore opens catalog read-only and does not call external project/batch reservation APIs. Its fresh catalog checks preserve explicit snapshots but do not prevent a subsequent catalog rename/deletion or prove cross-database reference protection.

owner_contracts.project_api: ProjectsStore::holdProjectReference(requestId,ownerModule,referenceKey,projectId) and releaseProjectReference(requestId,ownerModule,referenceKey); projectReferenceSucceeded/Error correlate by requestId and operation. checkProjectReferences returns exists plus references.
owner_contracts.batch_api: ReagentStore::holdBatchReference(requestId,ownerModule,referenceKey,batchId) and releaseBatchReference(requestId,ownerModule,referenceKey); batchReferenceSucceeded/Error correlate by requestId and operation. checkBatchReferences returns exists plus references.
owner_contracts.write_authority: Only the owning ProjectsStore/ReagentStore workers write their shared catalog tables. Calibration must invoke their value-based APIs through queued connections; it must not execute ad hoc shared-table SQL or share QSqlDatabase handles.

shell_write_gate_before_reference_coordi: Attach the independent page as read-only until reservation coordination, startup reconciliation and integration tests exist. Pass a calibration-local AccountSession copy with actionReady=false to CalibrationPage::setSession; this also queues the same session to CalibrationStore and prevents both UI and direct store writes. Keep real authentication fields truthful.

Do not enable local Save/New/Copy based only on a successful catalog load, a one-time reference query or an optimistic UI flag. Each write introducing a dependency needs an acknowledged durable reservation before the local record transaction.

The current page sends save/copy directly to CalibrationStore. Connecting it to a menu alone cannot insert the required reservation phase; introduce an explicit module coordinator or an equivalent checked write boundary before enabling editing in the shared-catalog program.

Keep catalog rename/delete operations affecting calibration-dependent IDs disabled during migration/backfill or when either store, reconciliation, reservation or release outcome is unknown. Existing standalone anonymous fixture testing remains an independent local slice, not proof of this shared-catalog protocol.
reservation_coordinator_integration_step: Choose ownerModule=calibration (valid lowercase module name). Persist a stable calibration database identity and stable reservation keys in calibration-owned metadata/intent storage before requesting holds. Do not derive keys from project names, table row positions, UI selection or a guessed next autoincrement ID. Current schema has no reservation-key linkage; this is required future integration work.

For a new or copied record, freeze project/batch IDs and immutable units/group snapshot as a value operation. Mark busy, reject duplicate requests, navigation and session changes until completion or explicit failure. Send holdProjectReference for the stable project ID; send holdBatchReference only when batchId>0. Wait for matching success signals for both reservations.

Same owner/key/ID holds are idempotent; rebinding a key to another ID fails. A failed, missing, locked, stale or permission-denied reservation must fail the write before local data commit, retain the draft and show the real error. No automatic retry or silent fallback to an unprotected write.

After all holds succeed, reread/validate the current committed catalog identity and units, then perform the calibration record/point transaction and durably link its reservation keys in calibration-owned storage. Catalog and calibration commits remain separate; do not describe them as one transaction or cross-file foreign keys.

For an update to an existing record, verify or restore its existing durable project/batch holds before accepting new raw points. Existing identity is immutable. Copy gets its own stable reservation ownership/key linkage or an explicitly reference-counted aggregate scheme; never release the source record's protection as part of copy failure.

If local save fails after holds, determine the final local outcome in the calibration worker, including retained hidden history and concurrent/pending operations. Release only reservations created exclusively for this failed operation and proven unused. If outcome is uncertain, preserve the safe blocking holds and record reconciliation work.

Current Delete is soft hiding: visible becomes0 but calibration_records and calibration_points remain. A hidden record still has historical project/batch references, so keep its reservations. General owner-contract release-after-delete instructions apply only after an approved physical purge removes every dependent local record/history and its transaction commits.

On restart, reconcile calibration-owned intents, visible and hidden records against owner reservations before allowing edits or affected catalog renames/deletions. Public CalibrationStore::load returns visible records only; reconciliation needs a dedicated bounded worker-side reference enumeration that includes hidden records. Never use GUI-thread SQL or automatically clear unknown/orphan holds.

Before enabling writes for pre-existing standalone data, freeze affected catalog changes and backfill project/batch reservations for all visible and hidden records. Missing or already-reused IDs require explicit reconciliation; an old display label alone is not authority to rebind history.

Call prepareToLeave before changing page, logout, relogin or application exit. Respect busy/draft refusal. Stop new coordinator operations, resolve/record pending outcomes, close databases on their owning workers, then quit/join threads.
required_integration_validation: Reserve project and batch, then verify rename/delete/group reassignment are rejected while visible and soft-hidden records exist; metadata-only edits follow the owner contract and never rewrite historical calibration values.

Locked/error/missing reservation APIs fail before local write; errors keep the draft. Repeated save and stale reservation replies cannot issue duplicate commits or attach holds to a later project/session.
Failure after only project hold, after both holds, during point insert and after local commit preserves/reconciles the correct reservations; retry uses stable keys and remains idempotent.
Restart at each inter-file boundary, then reopen visible and hidden history. Unknown outcomes remain blocked for reconciliation and do not auto-release protections.
Verify old executable rollback remains read-only with dependent external records because it may not enforce new catalog reference guards.

Run final unified Windows32 and ARM64 builds, original Windows same-state behavior/visual comparison, RK real screen, instrument/algorithm efficacy, resource budget and long stability separately. None is covered by this source review.
visual_source_fixes: calibrationchart.cpp now reserves90px left plot margin, moves the rotated y-axis title to its own left area and widens/repositions numeric tick labels so title and ticks have separate geometry. Rendering evidence belongs to the final rerun.
calibration_page.cpp gives disabled ordinary Apply buttons background#E4E4E4/text#AAAAAA from the existing source palette so unavailable actions are visibly disabled; no clinical action was enabled.
The modification date display uses original yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm:ss local-time formatting while its tooltip preserves the stored UTC ISO timestamp; storage stays explicit UTC.

Original active Windows theme/font/rendering and same-state visual parity remain unknown and require separate comparison. The original .ui hash and WSL screenshots do not establish active Windows equivalence.
unresolved_integration_obligations: Persistent project/batch reservation coordination remains unimplemented in the independent module; shared-catalog editing must stay gated until owner API holds and reconciliation are wired and verified.
Soft-hidden local records retain historical project/batch dependencies and their reservations must be retained.

Public CalibrationStore::load returns visible records only; startup/backfill reconciliation needs bounded worker-side enumeration including hidden records. No GUI-thread SQL or unverified release of holds.
